title: David and Jonathan
text:
After the young shepherd David killed Goliath, Jonathan, the son of King Saul and heir to the throne, loved him as his own soul. He made a covenant with David and gave him his own robe, his armor, his sword, his bow and his belt.

But as David's fame grew, Saul grew jealous and began trying to kill him. Jonathan spoke up for his friend and for a time persuaded his father to relent. When the danger returned, David hid in the countryside, and the two friends agreed on a signal. At the feast of the New Moon Jonathan would test his father's mood, then go out to the field where David was hiding and shoot arrows. If he called to the boy fetching them that they were beyond him, David must flee.

At the feast Saul noticed David's empty seat, and when Jonathan defended him, the king raged that as long as David lived, Jonathan would never be king. He even hurled his spear at his own son. The next morning Jonathan went to the field and shot the arrows, crying out that they were beyond the boy. Then he sent the boy home.

David came out of hiding. The two friends kissed each other and wept together, David most of all. "Go in peace," Jonathan told him, "for we have both sworn friendship in the name of the Lord."
lesson: A true friend wants good things for you even when your success costs him something. Be loyal in ways that are inconvenient, not only in ways that are easy.
